concepts.title: Economic and Non-Economic Activities
concepts.definition: Activities that create monetary value, like making furniture or flying planes, are economic activities; work done out of love or duty without payment, like teaching neighbourhood kids for free, is non-economic activity.
concepts.formula: economic = work + payment; non_economic = work without payment
concepts.key_idea: Money is the dividing line: the same skill, paid or unpaid, moves from market to service.

concepts.title: The Value of Work: Dignity in Every Task
concepts.definition: Every kind of honest work has worth, paid or unpaid; Swami Vivekananda's advice to do one's work as worship, and the respect owed to farmers, drivers, homema-kers and soldiers alike, ground this value.
concepts.key_idea: Work's worth is not measured by salary alone: effort, skill and service give every task dignity.

concepts.title: Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter
concepts.definition: Rajesh buys wood for 600 rupees and sells each chair for 1,000; the extra 400 rupees is the monetary value his skill, time and effort added, which is exactly what makes his work an economic activity.
concepts.key_idea: Value added is the measure of work: raw material in, a more valuable product out.

concepts.title: Work beyond Money
concepts.definition: The chapter honours work that payment cannot measure: a retired BSF grandfather teaching free geography classes, tending the vegetable garden, running errands, and homema-kers' daily care that holds a family together.
concepts.key_idea: A society runs on unpriced work too: care, teaching and service build the same wealth of trust.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is Rajesh's chair sold at 1,000 when the wood cost 600?

solution_template.explain: Wood in, 600 rupees; chair out, 1,000 rupees.
The 400 rupees pays for his skill, time and tools, the value his work added.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How is Geeta Aunty's flying different from her town's love for her?

solution_template.explain: Flying an Air Force plane is her paid profession; being the pride of the town is respect beyond money.
Work earns wages, but character and service earn honour.
